value: In this lesson, we solve a mystery: why does ‘hopping’ have two p's but ‘hoping’ has one?
But first, let's review some of the letters, sounds, and words we learned in previous lessons.
Before a word puts on an ‘-ing’ or ‘-ed’ ending, sometimes it changes a little first.
Change one: some words DOUBLE their last letter. ‘Hop’ becomes ‘hopping’.
Change two: Magic E words DROP their e. ‘Hope’ becomes ‘hoping’.
Here's the reading trick: a DOUBLED letter means the vowel stays short — ‘hopping’. A SINGLE letter is a clue there used to be a Magic E — so the vowel says its name: ‘hoping’!
Look closely at these two words. Two p's: short o — hopping, like a bunny. One p: long o — hoping, like making a wish!
Doubled letters — so every vowel here stays short. Read each word one beat at a time.
Single letters before the ending — the Magic E dropped off, but its spell remains! The vowel says its name.
